Wall-clock: 0.3 s sleeps against a 0.5 s deadline, asserting exactly two tracks ran. Under load the first track plus DB time can reach 0.5 s and only one runs. Patch time.monotonic with a fake clock, as the credits tests in the same file already do (_Clock).

83 inputs x every pattern x best-of-3 = 6.8 s. A super-linear pattern is slow on every run, so time each pattern once and re-time (best-of-3) only when it exceeds PATTERN_BUDGET_S to filter noise. Same detection at 100 KB, saving about 4 s. Do not shrink the 100 KB input: the budget is calibrated to it.

5.1 s: runs EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the frozen legacy SQL at 8000 tracks only to assert it loops 8000 times (a property of a static .sql file) and rows == 8000. The valuable assertion is that the new plan scans catalog_artists once; row equivalence with legacy is covered by test_input_query_preserves_rows_order_and_duplicate_cover_semantics. Drop the legacy run (and consider fewer tracks) to save about 4 s.

Mixes durable checks with per-release hand edits (a '1.x.0: file' list of module names, grep for 'def _drop_dj_tables') and a source-mode equality of __init__.py that goes red on every plugin commit and is already enforced, for the whole tree, by 'build_catalog.py --check' in CI. File-name pins cannot fail on a real defect since code_zip packs every file under the plugin dir. Keep: md5 of every archived version back to 1.2.4 (--check only covers the latest), PLUGIN_VERSION in the archive equals plugin.json's latest (no other test or --check compares them), no dj_ files.

Compares code_zip(working source) to the published zip, so in source mode it is red until each re-cut (the same property as CI --check, which it also calls at the end). code_zip sets create_system, date_time and external_attr explicitly, so the zipfile.sys monkeypatch is moot. Assert the platform-independent header fields and byte-identical output for a small synthetic tree under both patched platforms, with no dependency on the live release.

After monkeypatching HELPER_TURN_SECONDS to 0.3, 'HELPER_TURN_SECONDS < RUNNER_TURN_SECONDS' is a tautology; the real relation is never checked. Assert it on the shipped constants before patching. The elapsed < 3 s check is loose but wall-clock.

Disjointness and a single ender are the point and stay. But 'assert taken[r1] and taken[r2]' depends on thread scheduling (no sleep after a successful take, so one thread can drain all 14 batches). Add a small hold per batch, or drop that line.

Real pre-K10 golden, but the LUM-014 step runs PROVIDER_ALBUM_ID.sub over every section while only album rows were verified, so a changed provider_album_id on tracks or artists is rewritten to null and hidden. Three stacked strippers plus one whole-transcript equality give a single unreadable diff. Compare per label and restrict the sub to album rows.
Overruled: mutation run. Dropping the ensure_index call at journeys.py:62 is caught only by this test; 51 other tests run that line and stay green.
Overruled: mutation run. Dropping the ensure_index call at vibes.py:50 is caught only by this test; 47 other tests run that line and stay green.
Parity guard: the one-decode bundled path must equal the separate calls across 44.1k, 96k resample and mono.
Orphaned analysis children (PDEATHSIG) when the host job is OOM-killed or cancelled; proven with a real SIGKILL of a parent process on both transports.
Fork child using or closing the parent's shared Postgres socket after crash, signal, MemoryError and kill paths; real PG session proves protocol intact.
Hung decoder never reaped: asserts category, pid really gone, bounded elapsed time and that no path leaks into diagnostics.
The edge case where the track has no profile rows when the refresh starts, so any pre-lock filter on 'tracks with profiles' would miss it; only an interleaving test can see it.
Reproduces the exact lock-order interleaving that deadlocks under FOR SHARE on catalog_state; pins the FOR UPDATE decision with a real concurrency scenario instead of grepping SQL text.

Real two-connection race between a completion for an old media revision and a publication; checks nothing stays published, the withdrawal is journaled last and the attempt is fenced, in both interleavings. Stale-waveform-served-to-phone class.

Replaces the per-track implementation with a set-based one and proves row-for-row and journal-order equivalence across every state combination (including collation-order of delete events, other-source isolation, full_reconcile). Data-corruption class.

Re-runs the lookup's statements under EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on an unanalysed uncommitted generation and bounds buffers; protects the planner behaviour that made a refresh take 41-58 s. Not observable by any functional test.
Hooks a compaction commit into the middle of a reader's page for 3 streams and both timings. A reader must get a 410 or a dense page, never a silently short one.
Two threads with a held late commit: guards the global feed frontier against skipped events, a concurrency bug line coverage does not show.
Measures the time the feed head is held during a large chunked restore and the statements allowed inside it; a lock-hold budget (LUM-004) not expressible any other way.
Injects a refresh between the batch SELECT and DELETE on a real table; guards the repeated age filter that stops a live idempotency receipt being deleted.

About 100 seeded retry states built from the production retry-category sets, compared with fetch_backfill_rows, so the diagnostics page counts cannot drift from what the scheduler actually runs (a new retry category is covered automatically).
Query-plan regression (EXPLAIN) that keeps a 94k-track sweep off a seq scan of the whole job table.
New cursor-paged backfill candidate query vs the legacy query for every edge/job state combination and every paging boundary.
Cross-implementation golden shared with the TypeScript scorer; a ranking drift breaks federation parity.
Bounded DDL retry: attempts, backoff, log line, caller's lock_timeout restored and schema rolled back. A concurrency/rollback property no unit test can show.
Observes real lock modes from a second connection during a re-run migration (with a non-vacuity check). Catches ACCESS EXCLUSIVE/SHARE lock regressions that stall startup behind readers.
An idle runner turn creeping back to dozens of queries per tick (59 before WP4); counts real statements.
EBU Tech 3341 conformance numbers for integrated loudness; shows the BS.1770 meter is correct, not just that code runs.
EBU Tech 3342 loudness-range conformance; a gating or percentile error shows here and nowhere else.
a failed ping must not downgrade a blocked/pending transition or replace its required_action; losing it would re-publish a re-keyed library as removals

Protects the provider-identity transition shield: while the transition is pending, catalog and analysis admission must be denied with blocker 'provider_identity_transition' even when readiness says ready and acknowledged. Failure would let clients sync against a re-keyed server.
Protects restore integrity: a missing or mismatched checksum is rejected, and restored item ids are regenerated so a restore cannot collide with the source. Pairs with the duplicate-membership test.

Protects per-user isolation on export routes: both /backup and /{id}/export must pass the session user's principal ('user:alice') to the exporter, and responses must be no-store attachments. A regression would leak another user's collections.
a secret (DSN) in a diagnostic exception must never reach the page
Real Postgres, fault injected after the journal write. Protects publish atomicity: no edge row and head_seq unchanged after rollback, so a half-published profile cannot appear on the stream.

Real Postgres. Protects the edge payload being identical across direct read, bootstrap and /changes, a single journal seq, no media path leaking, and a repeat publish returning False. A bug here makes clients diverge silently.
re-key rewriting of plugin state must match whole values only and refuse a key collision, or it corrupts data silently
hex-encoded ping password in the Navidrome URL must be redacted from the identity card
classification of provider ID sets (detected, unchanged, conflict, incomplete) decides whether publication is blocked
the 1.5.0 incident: a slow ping stored transition_pending and every projection retry failed; asserts the row stays normal and the next good ping clears last_error

Real Postgres, 4 variants (legacy vs source-scoped tables, with and without media_fp). Protects the starvation bug where limit-1 backfill keeps returning ready rows with missing signatures and never reaches later stale rows. Note it builds minimal hand-written tables rather than using migrated_db.

Real Postgres. Protects the upgrade path: re-running migrate_enrichment on a relationship state at algorithm_version 0 marks it 'stale' but keeps result_generation 5, so clients keep serving the last published generation instead of an empty one.
a partially or wrongly library-mapped scan must not publish a catalogue
a refresh with an unverifiable provider version must still inspect ID sets, or re-keyed IDs publish as mass deletions plus additions
Real Postgres. Protects against serving an edge analysed for an old media file after the track was replaced, including a second replacement after a successful publish.
real Postgres: drops only the retired DJ tables and cron rows (LIKE underscore wildcard case), idempotent, keeps profiles/source tables
an aborted Postgres transaction after a failed status query must be rolled back before later panels read

Compares the streaming analyzer's ref_lufs and both ramps against an independent pure-Python biquad and chunk reference on a stereo signal. Protects loudness numerics and the stored v1 ramp bytes from drift.

Splits the same audio at 7777-sample blocks (with a 117-sample ragged tail) and requires bit-identical lufs and ramps. Protects filter-state and chunk carry-over bugs that only show up with real decoder block sizes.

Guards the opposite failure of the lock-avoidance work: if the 'skip DDL when nothing is missing' checks get too eager, older installs silently keep an old schema. Undoes about 40 objects and requires migrate to restore an identical schema.

Observes pg_locks from a second session while migrate reruns on an up-to-date database and fails on any lock stronger than ROW EXCLUSIVE, which would block live readers on every restart. Includes a non-vacuous check.
PyAV 16 SIGSEGV on planar 7.1/5.1 decode; run in a real child so a native crash fails the test, not the run.
The 1.8.0 livelock: a file longer than a tick is cancelled and restarted every tick so the pass never ends; real analysis children and real schema.
Mutates data from a second connection between batches. The capture must stay on one REPEATABLE READ snapshot, including the Python fallback rows, and snapshot_seq must not move.

EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a fresh snapshot table without statistics: the edge lookup must run at most page_size times, not once per remaining row. A pure query-plan regression that no output assertion would see.
Compares the SQL capture to the frozen Python oracle column by column: JSONB text (number scale), raw page bytes, and several batch sizes. Catches wire drift that a semantic comparison would miss.
Captures the publication DELETE and asserts no OR plus a plan with no Seq Scan that uses profile_changes_pkey on a 51k-row journal.
Real EXPLAIN of the exact statement: catalog_tracks must be reached through a Limit, per row. The earlier join took 20 s at 132k tracks, and output assertions would not catch a return to it.
Checked-in goldens from the pre-K6 server. An old client without the opt-in must get byte-identical /changes, catch-up and snapshot responses.
Removing the FOR UPDATE on the profile stream head failed only 1 of 39 tests before this module. Proves with pg_blocking_pids that the second append waits in its head read, so seqs stay dense.
Compaction, which never takes catalog_state, must wait for an append's head and must not compute the floor from a stale head. Asserts the exact floor (head-1000).
Fault injection at every statement boundary of the edge publisher on real transactions (not a fake DB). Nothing is half-published, and a retry then succeeds with seq 1.
ReDoS in the secret/path redaction regexes (a past 17 s hang) with an alarm so a regression fails rather than hangs.
Two runners running overlapping backfill batches, or a track analysed twice; checks the coalesced path.
Two runners on two connections claiming the same waiting request twice (claim race).
A NOTIFY read off the LISTEN connection during a turn is lost, so a forced rebuild waits 35 s for the next heartbeat; needs a real PostgreSQL socket.
The projection commit check missing a running AudioMuse id-rewrite or a held advisory migration lock, and rewriting IDs under it; the real advisory lock is the point.
Leader and helper admitting the same waveform track at once, so it is downloaded and analysed twice.
A batch orphaned by a dead runner never being redone, leaving a pass that cannot complete.
Concurrent slot acquisition over-subscribing the cross-runner files-in-flight cap.

Oracle test: the committed-summary readiness equals the old live-query readiness at every state reached the way the plugin reaches it, with live fallback forbidden. Wrong readiness blockers or admission shown to clients.
The panel reporting about 2,890 left for nine days because it read planner reltuples; depends on real Postgres statistics.

Runs the real 1.2.5 archive's writer against the current schema and shows its whole publication rolls back while the current publisher is unaffected. Corruption by a still-running old worker during a rolling restart.
Real planner behaviour under default statistics, with a guard that the pathological plan is reproducible; protects against a slow-search regression while results stay correct.
Pins index definitions and plans on the real migration; a dropped or reordered index silently makes search a seq scan.
Oracle comparison against the old queries across accent and case; a new search path cannot silently change results.
